one_line: Sanskrit court poet of the early Kadamba dynasty, who crafted the polished Talagunda pillar inscription.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, slim but sturdy scholar’s build, average height.
appearance.face: Oval face with a calm, thoughtful expression; medium-brown Deccan complexion; straight nose, defined cheekbones, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache; sharp, observant eyes that soften when he smiles.
appearance.hair: Dark brown-black hair, oiled and smoothed back into a short, tidy knot at the back of the head (early topknot), with a thin center part; simple narrow white cloth headband tied around the forehead, knot at the back, ends tucked.
appearance.costume: A modest early-5th-century Deccan Brahman scholar’s outfit: upper body wrapped in a soft, off-white cotton uttariya draped over both shoulders and chest like a shawl, with the end falling over the left arm; lower body in a plain, ankle-length dhoti of the same off-white cotton, neatly pleated in front and tied at the waist; a thin, pale saffron angavastra (scarf) folded and slung from the right shoulder under the uttariya edge; simple leather sandals on the feet; minimal jewellery limited to a single small copper bangle on the right wrist and a thin black-thread waist cord faintly visible at the tied dhoti edge.
appearance.signature: A smooth, rectangular palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with dark cord and held in his left hand, with a slender iron stylus tucked under the cord, the bundle edges slightly darkened from use.

ref_desc: Kubja of Talagunda is a medium-brown, oval-faced Sanskrit poet with a short beard, dark hair in a neat back knot with a white headband, wearing off-white dhoti and uttariya with a pale saffron scarf and copper bangle, holding a palm-leaf manuscript bundle with stylus.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Kubja of Talagunda, a mid-30s Sanskrit court poet from early 5th-century Deccan: medium-brown complexion, oval face with sharp, observant eyes and a calm, thoughtful default expression, straight nose, defined cheekbones, and a neatly trimmed short beard and moustache. His dark brown-black hair is oiled and smoothed into a small knot at the back of the head with a thin center part, and a narrow white cloth headband wraps his forehead with the knot hidden at the back. He wears an era-accurate, modest Brahman scholar outfit: a soft off-white cotton uttariya wrapped over both shoulders and chest like a shawl, its end falling over his left arm; a matching off-white, ankle-length dhoti, neatly pleated in front and tied at the waist; and a thin pale saffron angavastra folded and slung from the right shoulder under the edge of the uttariya. His feet are in simple leather sandals, and his only ornament is a single small copper bangle on the right wrist, with a thin black-thread waist cord just hinted at where the dhoti ties. In his left hand he carries his signature prop: a smooth rectangular palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with dark cord, edges slightly darkened from use, with a slender iron stylus tucked under the cord; his right hand can rest loosely by his side or lightly adjust the manuscript. Use a restrained, scholarly palette of off-white for garments, pale saffron for the scarf, dark brown-black for hair, medium brown for skin, and a soft copper tone for the bangle and stylus, and present him front and slightly angled views to clearly show his consistent face, hair knot with headband, wrapped garments, and the manuscript bundle.
